findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 3a056ea6eaf55acdc582f103f09a1c19f077200541f1ccf4880cbbb7c93a8133; all 6 declared sources passed current HTTPS access review.
Claims remain bounded to current Texas recording and copy statutes plus current Tarrant and Harris County Clerk search, access, certification, fee, and limitation examples.

The article invents no county, person, entity, instrument, document number, recording date, volume or page, legal description, property, ownership fact, deed meaning, tax fact, amount, offer, calculation, or professional conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Property Code Chapter 11, §11.001 (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Property Code Chapter 11, including §11.001, supplies the county-of-recording context for an eligible real-property instrument.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It supports office-identification context only. It does not identify the correct instrument for an owner, determine current ownership or title, interpret a deed, establish completeness, or support a tax, valuation, offer, or transaction conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Local Government Code Chapter 191, §§191.004 and 191.0041 (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Local Government Code §§191.004 and 191.0041 supply the attested-copy obligation, fee context, and elements required for a certified copy made from an original document on file with a county clerk.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: They support plain-versus-certified source context only. The article does not choose a copy type, claim certification proves ownership or legal effect, or decide whether a copy is sufficient for a professional purpose.

sources_inspected.label: Tarrant County Clerk, Copies of Official Public Records (Real Property) (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current Tarrant County Clerk page supplies four copy routes, free unofficial watermarked-copy context, online certified-copy routing, current in-person and mail copy-fee examples, and the no-title-search or restriction-determination boundary.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It supports a dated county example only. The article does not generalize Tarrant methods or fees statewide, purchase a copy, promise availability, conduct a title search, or determine restrictions.

sources_inspected.label: Tarrant County Clerk, Central Library FAQs (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current Tarrant County Central Library FAQ confirms that deeds and related real-estate records can be printed or certified, that the public may use the designated official-records search, and that staff do not provide legal advice or perform the user's search.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It supports current navigation and professional-boundary context only. It does not establish which deed is operative, prove title, or authorize legal interpretation.

sources_inspected.label: Harris County Clerk, Real Property Document Search Portal (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current Harris County Clerk portal supplies supported real-property search fields, stated online image coverage, posting-delay context, the warning that the online database is not the official repository, and plain or certified copy ordering routes.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It supports a second current county example and negative-result limitations only. The article does not treat its fields, range, delay, copy options, or certification format as universal.

sources_inspected.label: Harris County Clerk, Public Records Ordering Copies (accessed 2026-08-26)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current Harris County Clerk public-records page supplies free watermarked viewing, paper and electronic copy routes, current plain and certified fee examples, a search-fee condition, and the owner-name and legal-description deed-request context.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It supports a dated county example only. The article does not quote Harris fees as statewide, infer owner identity or a legal description, recommend purchasing a format, or claim the resulting copy resolves title or tax questions.
